_comment: COURT RECORDS. Read docs/SCRAPING.md before enabling any of these.
Two rules, and they are practical rather than preachy:
1. Prefer an official bulk data request. Tennessee probate clerks will often
provide filings on a schedule for a fee or a records request. That is more
reliable than scraping, needs no maintenance when the site is redesigned,
and removes the terms question entirely. Ask first, scrape second.
2. Never point a scraper at a portal you had to log into or click through an
agreement to reach. Public data on an open page is one thing. A subscriber
portal is a contract you agreed to, which is a different category of risk.
Davidson County's CaseLink is a subscriber service, so it is deliberately
The browser connector renders JavaScript locally with no scraping subscription.
It does not defeat CAPTCHAs or bot protection, and it should not be made to.
If a portal blocks automated access, that is the portal answering the question:

sources.name: probate-davidson
sources.label: Davidson County probate filings
notes: Davidson probate is handled by the Probate Court Clerk at 1 Public Square.
The clerk accepts a Probate Records Request Form, which is the better path.
CaseLink covers Circuit, Probate and General Sessions Civil but it is a
SUBSCRIBER tool. Do not scrape it. If you subscribe, export from inside it.
The steps array is a template. Open the public search in a normal browser,
right click the fields you fill in, copy their selectors, and paste them.
minIntervalMs is 2000. A court server is not an API.

sources.name: probate-williamson
sources.label: Williamson County probate, Chancery Clerk and Master
notes: In Tennessee probate sits in Chancery Court, so the office you want is the
Clerk and Master rather than the Circuit Court Clerk. It handles estate
administration, wills, guardianships and conservatorships.
The statewide portal at tncourts.gov is worth checking first, since one
source covering several counties beats one config per county.

sources.name: divorce-filings-template
sources.label: Divorce filings, NOT USABLE YET, see notes
notes: HONEST LIMITATION. This will not produce usable leads as the pipeline
stands, and enabling it would create junk rows.
A divorce docket publishes party names and a case number. It does not
publish a property address, because the property is described inside the
complaint or the final decree rather than in the docket listing.
Everything in this pipeline joins on address or parcel number. A record
with only names has nothing to join to, so it lands as an orphan row.
What is needed is owner name matching: normalize the docket parties and
look them up against owner_name on the parcel roll. That is a real feature
and not a large one, it just does not exist yet. Ask for it.
Also note divorce case contents are frequently sealed even where the docket
entry is public, and a divorce filing does not by itself mean a sale.
